A.explanation: Total sweep would be $10 \times 1 \text{ s} = 10 \text{ s}$, containing about 500 pulses of period $20 \text{ ms}$, so pulses merge together.

B.explanation: Total sweep is $10 \times 10 \text{ ms} = 100 \text{ ms}$, about five periods of $20 \text{ ms}$, so a few clearly separated pulses fit on the 10 cm screen.

C.explanation: Total sweep would be $10 \times 100 \text{ }\mu\text{s} = 1 \text{ ms}$, much less than one $20 \text{ ms}$ period, so a pulse will usually not even appear.

D.explanation: Total sweep would be $10 \times 1 \text{ }\mu\text{s} = 10 \text{ }\mu\text{s}$, far shorter than the $20 \text{ ms}$ between pulses, so no pulse is displayed.

hints: Convert the flywheel speed of 3000 revolutions per minute into revolutions per second to find how often magnet M passes the coil.
Use that pulse frequency to find the time between pulses, then compare it with the 10 cm width of the c.r.o. screen.
Check the total time of one sweep, given by time-base setting multiplied by 10 cm, and look for a total time that holds a few pulse intervals.
walkthrough: One pulse is produced per revolution, so the pulse period equals the rotation period. Convert $3000 \text{ rev min}^{-1}$ to per second: $3000/60 = 50 \text{ rev s}^{-1}$.
Period $T = 1/f = 1/50 = 0.020 \text{ s} = 20 \text{ ms}$. This is the time between successive voltage pulses from the coil.
The horizontal sweep time across the whole screen is time-base $\times$ width. With width $= 10 \text{ cm}$, total time $= 10 \times$ time-base setting.
For clearly separate pulses, the total sweep should be a few times $20 \text{ ms}$, for example $40-100 \text{ ms}$, so about 2-5 pulses appear.
Testing $10 \text{ ms cm}^{-1}$ gives $10 \times 10 \text{ ms} = 100 \text{ ms}$, which is $5 \times 20 \text{ ms}$ and displays about five spaced pulses. This is option B.
